steps.text: Preheat the oven to 350 degrees F (175 degrees C). Generously grease a 9-inch springform pan with 2 3/4-inch sides.
Make crust: Mix together crushed cookies and butter in a medium bowl until well combined. Press mixture evenly into the prepared pan.
Bake in the preheated oven for 5 minutes. Set aside to cool.

Make filling: Combine 1 cup cream, chocolate chips, vanilla, and salt in the top of a double boiler. Heat, stirring occasionally, until chocolate is fully melted and mixture is smooth. Pour chocolate mixture into a large bowl; cool to room temperature, stirring occasionally.

Beat 2 cups cream in a second large bowl until stiff peaks form. Fold into chocolate mixture until well combined. Pour mixture into cooled crust. Chill pie in the refrigerator for at least 6 hours before topping and serving.
Make topping: Beat chilled cream and sugar with an electric mixer in a medium bowl until stiff. Pipe onto the top of pie with a star tip, or spoon dollops onto each slice to serve.

raw_recipe.headline: Death by Chocolate Mousse
raw_recipe.description: This chocolate mousse pie topped with whipped cream features a luscious filling in a rich cookie crust for a decadent and dazzling holiday dessert.

video.description: So easy to make, this rich pie will be devoured and requested over and over. Crush chocolate sandwich cookies and mix with softened butter, then press into a pan and bake. Create a creamy filling by melting chocolate chips with heavy cream and vanilla. Then cool and blend with whipped cream and sugar and pour into the cooled crust. Chill and top with sweetened whipped cream, then grab your slice quickly, because everyone will fight to the death for every last bite of this dangerously dreamy dessert!

review.reviewBody: This was so easy and so GOOD!! I made it even easier by doing step 3 in the microwave instead of a double boiler--just combine the chocolate and cream and heat at 1-minute intervals, stirring in between, until the chocolate is melted. Also, I made this for Thanksgiving and my mom doesn't like to eat a lot of sugar, so I used unsweetened chocolate (good quality, of course, is key) and Splenda (probably about 1/3 C). It turned out great. Oh, and also I used a regular pastry pie crust instead of the cookie crust. I think it was definitely the way to go. The filling is so rich, I think the cookie crust would have been too much. I think this recipe will become a new holiday tradition. Thanks!!

Fabulous. A wonderful addition is espresso powder! Add it to the chocolate while melting (I used about a teaspoon)...it adds a little depth of flavor that is amazing to an already great recipe! I also HIGHLY suggest using chocolate in bar form (such as Ghiradelli), because it melts much better than chips. Not only does bar chocolate have more cocoa butter, causing it to melt better, but chips have additives that are there to help them hold their shape by raising their melting temperature (why they are perfect for chocolate chip cookies), making them not the best tasting chocolate for melting either- partly because of the additives and partly because chocolate flavonoids are highly volatile and the less heat chocolate is subjected to the better it will taste.

Oh my this is so good! I used the food processor method and this went together super fast. I did use chocolate grahams instead of the cookies. Also instead of white sugar I used powdered sugar. It mixes in much better with the heavy cream than regular sugar does. Came out perfect! Thanks.
Delicious and decadent.......I just made the mousse and placed it in martini glasses.....added some strawberries and the whipped cream. Elegant presentation and divine taste!

AMAZING! Instead of the Oreo crust, I took my favorite chocolate cake recipe, divided it into thirds, and baked in a 9-in round pan, which I cooled and put in the bottom of the springform pan. My guests couldn't have eaten more than 1/12 of the cake/mousse.

I made this recipe exactly how it was written and my family looooved it! I made it the second time and instead of cookies for a crust, I used brownies instead and put them in individual cups to manage servings. I shaved a hershey chocolate bar and sprinkled some on the top of the whipped cream. This is my go to chocolate dessert for the holidays and it NEVER disappoints!

This came out delicious and everyone is asking for the recipe. Only added a layer of raspberry filling to the bottom (1/4c sugar, 1T cornstarch, 2t water; 2c fresh raspberries over med heat x 5 min, add 1/4 t almond extract at end, remove from heat cool then chill). Really gave the pie the perfect touch and broke up the sweetness perfectly!

Omg, it was so good! I was lazy and used a pre-made crust and topped it with cool whip, but it was still delicious! Everyone fought over who got to take the leftovers home. I've used a different recipe from this website for a chocolate pie several times, but I happened upon this one, and decided to use it instead. It's so much better. I didn't realize it was so easy to make chocolate mousse. The recipe made more than what would fit in the pie crust, and I didn't know what to do with the extra...yeah, I ended up just eating it from a bowl with a spoon because it was so yummy. Definitely making it again for the next get together with friends or family. Btw, I didn't use a double boiler, I just melted the chocolate with the cream in a pot on the stove on low heat, and it turned out fine.

This is absolutely delicious! It was very easy to make and I prepared almost exactly as described. The only change I would recommend is that if you are using Oreos for your crust, you won't need an entire stick of butter. I softened a stick but then blended in a little at a time and probably only ended up using about 3 tbs. baking the crust allows it to hold together quite nicely and 5 minutes is the perfect amount of time. I also followed 2 review suggestions. I used high quality bar chocolate (Trader Joe's dark chocolate) and espresso powder (Starbucks Via). I dissolved about a half packet of Via in a small amount of the cream and added it to the melted chocolate mixture. This is a wonderful recipe.

This recipe is very good, but also quite rich. I doubled the cookie crust based on others' comments and it was a bit too thick, so I think 1 1/2 times the crust recipe would've been best. I flavored the whipped cream topping with 4 Tablespoons of Hazelnut Kahlua liqeur and reduced the sugar to 2 Tablespoons -- came out great. I topped it with fresh raspberries and lightly toased, finely chopped pecans. It wowed my guests. I will definitely make this again. This dessert tastes best when served closer to room temp (but still slightly chilled) -- the texture is more creamy and silky. (You can also find this recipe on epicurious.com -- it's called "chocolate mousse pie.")

Didn't have a spring form pan, so I used extra oreos and made a full chocolate crumb pie crust. USED the microwave method, but would stir every 30 seconds once we were getting close to melted. Didn't want the chocolate to break. This was phenomenally delicious, and I orally don't like rich chocolate stuff. the ores and whipped cream topping were a perfect balance to the dark chocolate. This is going in my recipe bible!

I have been making this pie for family and friends for the past six years. Every time the holidays come around they request that I make this pie. It is absolutely delicious and you won’t be disappointed.
No raw eggs or messing w gelatin!

I have made this multiple times following the recipe exactly, my family and co-workers love it. I have also adjusted the recipe by replacing the chocolate chips with dark chocolate chips and adding cherry pie feeling to the whipped topping.

I made this for Thanksgiving and an office holiday potluck. Both times I got a lot of compliments on it and requests to make it again. It was so good and the recipe was easy to follow. The only thing I did different was use powdered sugar instead of granulated sugar in the whipped topping for more stability and smoother texture.
Incredible! Used oreo cookie crumbs for crust.
